subject: general
question: The prohibition of human trafficking has been laid under _______ in the Indian Constitution.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 23**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Human trafficking**

 
 
• Human trafficking involves the **exploitation** of others for one's **own gain or for money**.
 
• The victims are put through **fraud or compulsion **in order to engage in commercial sex, debt slavery, or forced labour.
 
• The Indian Constitution's **Articles 23 and 24** provide the **right against exploitation**.
 
• These crucial fundamental rights guarantee that no citizen will be subjected to any form of forced labour.
 
• **Article 23 (1) **of the Indian Constitution forbids the **trafficking of Human Beings** or Persons. 
 
• In Article 23(1) it is stated that **trafficking in human beings, begging for money, and other similar types of forced labour are forbidden, and any violation of this rule is a crime subject to legal sanctions**.
 
• According to **Article 24**, no kid under the age of fourteen may work in any dangerous occupation, such as a mine or a factory.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Human trafficking laws in India**

 
 
• Indian Penal Code, 1860
 
• The Indian Penal Code, 1860 governs how human trafficking is generally dealt with in India.
 
• Immortal Traffic (Prevention) Act, 1956 (ITPA)
 
• Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2013
 
• Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act, 2012
 
 
 
• Other special laws against trafficking in children and women have been passed such as the **Child Labor (Prohibition and Regulation) Act of 1986, Prohibition of Child Marriage Act of 2006, Transplantation of Human Organs Act of 1994, and Bonded Labor System (Abolition) Act of 1976**.
 
• According to **Article 21**, the State may not take away someone's life or personal liberty unless it follows a certain legal process.
 
• The protection against arrest and detention in specific circumstances is covered by **Article 22**.
